question: Will H.R. 33 (United States–Taiwan Expedited Double-Tax Relief Act) be enacted into law before May 1, 2026?
summary: House passage by a wide margin and a Senate companion introduce real bicameral momentum that could lift enactment odds.
Implementing legislation plus a bilateral tax agreement adds a multi-step process with potential delays, risking missing the May 1 target.
Historical enactment rates for federal legislation are low (~6%), creating a downward bias on timely enactment.
Overall, momentum provides upside but structural friction and uncertain Senate fate keep the probability modest; calibrated around 14% (roughly 8–22%).
